His lift routine looks good, but if you want to build muscle I wouldn't do as much cardio as the rock did. He was probably cutting body fat to look ripped on screen. Keep in mind that 9 hours of exercise per week is a lot, especially with something as exhausting as weight training. And the rock is a professional athlete with the resources to balance that amount of activity with the rest of his schedule. 1 hour of cardio a week vs the rocks 3 hours should help your results if you want to build muscle. And you can use the spare time for eating or grocery shopping.

Gym etiquette is simple, be polite, be careful of people lifting, put away your weights, clean up sweat, etc. YouTube can teach you how to do the rocks lifts, or if you want you can hire a trainer. There's going to be some impressive physiques in the weight areas, these men and women have been lifting for years so you can ask them questions if they don't look that busy. Most people just stick to themselves though. Don't worry at all about your fitness level, everybody started somewhere.

Food is your priority over supplements. It's better to buy 50 dollars of groceries vs a tub of protein powder.

Low fat low carb is a classic stumbling block. My maintenance diet has over 300 grams of carbs and over 100 grams of fat. Your body needs all three macros in large quantities to get big.

6 days a week and 7 lifts per session? That might burn you out really fast. That sort of routine is made for someone who either doesn't have a job or does have a job lifting weights (like The Rock or a personal trainer). Most programs do 3-4 days a week with 3-6 lifts per session. It looks like you want a body building split routine, so I want throw the standard beginner strength programs at you. Take a look at Lyle McDonald's Generic Bulking Routine as an example of a more manageable body building split.

Also, the whole "squats are rough on your knees" thing is a highly contentious issue (Do I dare say it is debunked myth?). If you're trying to protect a bad knee, I don't see how squats would be any worse for you than leg presses. The quadriceps are extending the knee in the same way during both exercises.

Finally, I'll sign off with one tip. If you're a beginner weightlifter, don't necessarily try to copy what the really jacked guys are doing. What is good for an advanced lifter is often not a good choice for a beginner.

Stacksity

  • https://stacksity.com
  • Finished product. Works well, seems to have a solid code and behind the scenes stuff.
  • Voaters and Redditors will be able to use it intuitively
  • Similar in organization to Voat. Main difference is that subforums (called Stacks) cannot be moderated. Only voting mechanism is the moderator.
  • Requires email on login, but can be bogus, it is not validated
  • Can host images directly, not only links.
  • Nothings seems to be removed, no censorship.
  • Has four categories of visibility. Safe, NSFW, Nudity and Gore. Great idea if you ask me!

Frizbee

  • https://frizbee.co
  • Still beta. Usable but needs some polishing and further work.
  • Friendly mods that are actually interested in your feedback
  • Very anti-censorship, anti tracking focused. User accounts are not needed, you can post by anonymous. The manifesto professes dedication to free speech, so no banning or censoring will ever occur. Warning: not protecting your account means somebody else can take it later!
  • The page settings and orientation of elements is unusual and needs to be learned. I think reorganization will happen in the future.
  • Quite unique decentralization project. Some content can be hosted on different servers, not the ones rented by Frizbee directly. So no entire stack can be banned.

Snapzu

  • http://snapzu.com/
  • Most technologically advanced of all
  • Does have unique karma system where you progress through level as if you were in RPG
  • Resembles Pinterest the most, you can switch between reddit-like view of links and Tumblr-like tiles
  • The subforums are called tribes and moderator of the forum is tribe chief.
  • I find the site not having any edge, any bite.
  • Probably aimed at soccer moms and similar crowd. Very middle-of-the-road community.
  • Their user agreement basically says "do not post anything controversial ever"

Aether

  • http://getaether.net
  • Works as an application on Peer-to-peer basis. You intall Aether on your computer. Later, you will find a link there and open it in your browser.
  • Stores only links, not even image thumbnails.
  • Technically works very well.
  • Anti-censorship focused. Literary impossible to policy, even more so than Frisbee. May be useful for users in authoritative countries.
  • You have no claim to your username. Anyone can impersonate you if they wish.
  • Only aggregator that can work for the deep web.
  • Desperately needs more users and content.

  • Minimal interface, no ads, several colour themes
  • Voting on post/comment = "I want to share this with others on Hubski", rather than "I agree" or "I find this relevant"
  • No negative voting, score only goes up, and up to a cap, denoted by a maximum number of dots around a circle per post/comment
  • No subforum divisions; posts have #tags instead
  • Rather than subscribing, users either follow specific #tags or other users to see the relevant posts in their main feed
  • Each user profile displays his/her stats - followers, posting/sharing activity, recent posts/shares etc.
  • "Zen mode" is special: enabling it completely disables post/comment score AND user stats
